title: Simplex
subtitle: Write your linear programming problem below or load it from a file.

hint.bigM: Artificial variables with a very large penalty $M$ in the objective function.
hint.twoPhase: Phase I finds a feasible solution; Phase II solves the original problem.
hint.generalized: Only ≤ constraints, no artificial variables; uses dual simplex rules when the right-hand side is negative.

setup.title: Model setup
setup.bigM: Every constraint becomes an equality: ≤ constraints get a slack variable ($s$); ≥ constraints get a surplus variable ($e$) and an artificial one ($a$); = constraints get an artificial one. Artificials enter the objective with the penalty $M = {{m}}$, which forces them to 0 at the optimum.
setup.twoPhase: Every constraint becomes an equality: ≤ gets slack ($s$); ≥ gets surplus ($e$) and artificial ($a$); = gets artificial. Phase I minimizes $w = \sum a_i$ (the sum of the artificials). If the minimum is 0 the model is feasible and Phase II solves the real problem.
setup.twoPhaseNoArtificial: All constraints are ≤, so there are no artificial variables and Phase I is not needed: the problem is solved directly.
setup.generalized: Every constraint becomes ≤: a ≥ constraint is multiplied by −1 and an equality becomes two inequalities (≤ and ≥ multiplied by −1). Then each row gets a slack variable. There are no artificial variables; negative right-hand sides are repaired with dual simplex rules.

step.title: What happened in this iteration
step.canonical: Before optimizing, basic variables must have coefficient 0 in row $z$. {{col}} is basic but has a non-zero coefficient, so it is eliminated from row $z$ using row {{row}}.
step.entersMostNegative: Entering variable: the most negative coefficient in row $z$ is {{value}}, in the column of {{col}}.
step.entersMostPositive: Entering variable: since row $z$ is shown with the sign flipped (minimization), the most positive coefficient counts: {{value}}, in the column of {{col}}.
step.dual: Row {{row}} has a negative right-hand side ({{rhs}}) — the solution is not feasible yet. By the dual simplex rules that is the leaving row. The entering variable is the one with the smallest ratio $|c_j / a_{ij}|$ among the negative coefficients of the row: {{col}}.
step.leaves: Leaving variable: the smallest ratio $b_i / a_{ij}$ among the positive coefficients of the column of {{col}} is {{ratio}}, in row {{row}} — {{leaving}} leaves.
step.degenerate: There is a tie in the minimum ratio among rows {{rows}}: the solution is degenerate. The first one leaves the basis and the others get right-hand side 0.
step.unbounded: All coefficients in the column of {{col}} are less than or equal to 0: no row limits the growth. The objective grows without bound (unbounded solution).
step.infeasible: No variable can enter the basis and the solution is still infeasible: the problem has no feasible solution.
step.noOperations: The other rows already have 0 in the pivot column.
step.phase2Start: End of Phase I: $w = 0$, so the original model is feasible. The artificial columns were removed and the original objective function was restored.
step.phase1Infeasible: End of Phase I: the minimum of $w$ is greater than 0, so the original model has no feasible solution.
step.optimal: Stopping condition: no coefficient in row $z$ can improve the objective and all right-hand sides are non-negative — this tableau is optimal.
step.clickHint: Tip: click a positive number in the table to choose the pivot yourself.
